note: Fictional communities and pseudonymous posts written by Foothold; no real people.

circles.name: Students figuring it out
circles.description: High schoolers and first-year college students comparing paths.

posts.text: Signed up for my first dual-enrollment class at Delta. Kind of nervous about being the youngest in the room.
You'll be fine. I did precalc there junior year; the professor cared more that you showed up than how old you were.
Tip for anyone taking the bus: I do my reading on the ride. 35 minutes each way adds up.
Does anyone else feel behind because they didn't start coding at 10? Started at 16 and it's going okay.
Totally normal. Most people in my CS class started in high school or later.
Anatomy lab is hard but the study group on Thursdays is saving me.
Update: survived week one. The counselor helped me map which classes transfer. ASSIST is confusing but worth it.
First in my family doing college stuff. Asking questions in office hours felt weird at first, now it's my favorite part.

circles.name: Career changers
circles.description: Adults switching fields, often while working full-time.

posts.text: Warehouse brought in the new picking robots. Instead of panicking I asked the tech what training he had.
Started an evening PLC class at 41. My kids quiz me on ladder logic now, it's hilarious.
Hardest part for me is the schedule. Two kids, 45 hours a week. I take one class at a time and that's okay.
One class at a time still gets you there. Took me three semesters for my first certificate.
Went back for prereqs at 38 for nursing. The younger students ask me for help with time management.
Anyone know if employers count sim results or just certificates? Asking before I spend money.
Some do both. Mine cared a lot about the safety record I already had.
Reminder to rest. We're doing two jobs: working and learning.

circles.name: Trades crew
circles.description: Diesel, welding, electrical and ag mechanics folks.

posts.text: Rebuilt a hydraulic pump with my uncle this weekend. Want the certificate so customers trust the shop.
SMAW cert test is next month. Practicing verticals every night after work.
Got into the apprenticeship interview round. The algebra requirement was the scary part, glad I did it.
Congrats! What did they ask in the oral interview?
Mostly why I wanted the trade and how I handle safety. Be honest and specific.
Air brakes class was way more math than I expected. Worth it though.
Shoutout to the open lab hours. Free practice time makes a huge difference.
Remember to ask about tool programs. Some shops help with tool costs.

circles.name: Parents and caregivers
circles.description: Learning while caring for kids or family.

posts.text: Online sections are the only reason I can take classes. Studying after bedtime.
Found a Saturday hybrid class so my partner covers mornings. Small wins.
Taking care of my mom and taking a spreadsheet course. Slow but steady.
Some days I only get 20 minutes in. Counting those as progress now.
The campus has a childcare center, ask about it. I didn't know for a whole semester.
Feeling guilty about time away from family. Anyone else?
Yes. My kids told me they're proud of me. That helped.
Thanks all. Signing up for one class next term instead of two.
